policy_title: Strengthen and expand public NHS services
stated: Commit to increasing NHS annual expenditure, rising to £28bn by 2030, and £20bn in capital spending over five years for hospital building and repair, including an immediate budget increase for fair wage settlements for staff. This will reduce hospital waiting lists, guarantee rapid access to a GP (same-day for urgent needs), and ensure universal access to NHS dentistry with an additional £3bn a year by 2030. The policy also aims to restore public health budgets to 2015/16 levels with an immediate £1.5bn increase, properly funding services like smoking cessation, drug and alcohol treatment, and sexual health. It will introduce a National Cancer Control Plan to reduce cases, meet early diagnosis targets, and deliver treatment through publicly funded research. Investment will also improve mental health care access, ensuring evidence-based therapies within 28 days, with trained counsellors in every primary and secondary school. The NHS will be defended against privatisation by abolishing wasteful competition, re-establishing public bodies and accountability, restricting commercial companies, and backing the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

source.quote: We estimate that to meet these commitments, the NHS in England would require additional annual expenditure of £8bn in the first full year of the next parliament, rising to a total of £28bn in 2030. We also estimate that additional capital spending of at least £20bn is needed in total over the next five years. We will prioritise supporting NHS workers, including by providing an immediate one-off budget increase to cover fair wage settlements. We would bring down hospital waiting lists by giving Hospital Trusts clear, long-term, funding commitments, so that they can better plan to deliver better care for us all. Elected Greens will push for: • A steady reduction in waiting lists. • We would guarantee rapid access to a GP and same day access in case of urgent need. Elected Greens will push for a new contract for NHS dentists that ensures everybody who needs an NHS dentist has access to one. Additional investment in NHS dentistry, reaching £3bn a year by 2030, would transform the availability of appointments and end the scandal of dental treatment deserts. Elected Greens will campaign for funding to allow community hubs and primary care to provide a roll-out of free dental nursing for children and those on low incomes. Restoring public health budgets to 2015/16 levels with an immediate increase of £1.5bn. Smoking cessation, drug and alcohol treatment and sexual health services all need to be properly funded. Protect our NHS from privatisation – keep our NHS public abolish wasteful competition within the NHS, reestablish public bodies and public accountability, and restrict the role of commercial companies. Green MPs will back the NHS Reinstatement Bill to public health. We will commit to a National Cancer Control Plan to include: • Reducing cases through investment in public health measures, such as interventions on food, alcohol and tobacco. • Meet the existing NHS target of 75% of cases diagnosed at stage 1 or stage 2 by 2028 though investment in primary care and enhanced screening. • Using the unique information the NHS has, as a public health system that cares for us from cradle to the grave, to deliver treatment through publicly funded research. Elected Greens will focus on enabling major improvements to mental health care to put it on a truly equal footing with physical health care. This will include ensuring that everyone who needs it can access evidence-based mental health therapies within 28 days. We will provide a trained and paid counsellor in every primary and secondary school, and every sixth-form college.

consolidated_from: Increase NHS funding and staff pay
Reduce NHS waiting lists and guarantee GP access
Increase public health funding and establish a commission on drug law reform
Re-establish a fully public NHS and end privatisation
Implement a National Cancer Control Plan
Improve mental health care access and provision

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets NHS capacity, waiting lists, GP access, dental access, mental health, cancer care, and public health funding — all core healthcare access indicators.

An immediate budget increase for fair wage settlements for NHS staff (c.1.5 m employees in England) directly moves the real-wages indicator for a large workforce, making this a non-negligible O4 effect.

The policy mandates trained counsellors in every primary and secondary school, directly placing a health-and-wellbeing resource inside educational settings in a way that affects school attendance, attainment, and opportunity — a non-negligible school-level intervention.

The cumulative spending commitment (£28bn/year NHS by 2030, £20bn capital, £3bn/year dentistry, £1.5bn public health) is very large; the policy text does not specify the funding mechanism, making the impact on debt-path sustainability a real and non-negligible question warranting a verdict.

membership_note: Core bearing is O3 (the policy's explicit purpose); O4 is earned by the explicit staff pay commitment; O7 by the school-counsellor mandate; O12 by the very large and funding-unspecified spending total. No other fundamentals clear the non-negligible bar: inequality effects (O14) from NHS universalism are real but indirect relative to income/wealth-gap indicators; cost-of-living effects (O2) are secondary to the access mechanism already scored on O3.
